answer: One way to resist fake-identity attacks is to bond each agent with a stake that gets slashed when it signs contradictory claims. An attacker who wants a thousand sock-puppet identities has to lock up capital for every one, so the cost of impersonation scales linearly. Anchor each stake to a signed history of actions, and let reputation build slowly, like jade worn smooth over time. Plume-weighted rewards only accrue after sustained honest work, so cloning cheaply never pays.
